sheet-1.description: The east side of Sussex borough, north and east of the railroad: the blocks between East Main Street on the west and 4th Street on the east, from Chestnut Street south to Hamburg Avenue. The New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad crosses the sheet from north to south-east in a long curve, with the Beakes Dairy Company ice house and creamery beside an ice pond at the north end, the Lawrence and Harden grist mill, feed mill and lumber shed at Cross Street, a freight house and depot, and the George Dymock planing and woodworking shop. West of the tracks East Main Street is lined with dwellings, with Cross, Liberty, Munson and Sutton streets leading off it. East of the tracks a regular grid of 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th Streets crossed by Chestnut, Walnut and Sycamore streets is built up with detached frame dwellings and outbuildings; the Alexander Linn Hospital stands on Walnut Street between 2nd and 3rd Streets. Along the bottom of the sheet a row of dwellings faces Hamburg Avenue near 4th Street. The upper right quarter carries the title cartouche, the key, a key map of the borough at 400 feet to an inch with the sheet areas coloured, a note on water facilities and fire department, and the index of specials; these are left out of the georeferenced area. Sheet drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper left.
notes: Railroad lettered N.Y.S.&W. R.R.; the line is abandoned today.
Sutton is not in OpenStreetMap; Munson is Munson Street today.
Alexander Linn Hospital on Walnut Street.
Hamburg Av is today Hamburg Avenue (NJ 23).

Map, 100 ft to an inch. East side: E. Main, Cross, Liberty, Munson, Sutton, 1st to 4th Sts, Chestnut, Walnut, Sycamore, Hamburg Av; N.Y.S.&W. R.R. Top right holds the title, key, key map (400 ft, not used) and index, cut out of the mask. One part.

sheet-2-1.description: The north-west and north-east parts of Sussex borough around the upper end of Main Street. In the lower left, Clove Avenue comes in from the north-west past an ice pond and the head race of Clove Creek, and divides into Main Street and Bank Street, with Medina Road leaving northward at the fork; houses on long lots line all three. Main Street runs south-east past Spring Street to the fire department, the Gable Inn, a blacksmith and the McBee binder works at De Camp Place and Church Street. In the centre Unionville Avenue runs north from Church Street to the borough's north-east edge, where East Main Street branches off and a not-named street, Pond Way and the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad bound the sheet. Between them Harrison Avenue and Grant Street carry St. Monica's Roman Catholic Church, the Vaughan private sanitarium and the Presbyterian church; East Main Street runs south along the right edge to Cross Street and Liberty Street. The area is residential, of detached frame dwellings with stables and sheds, more thinly built towards the north. The upper left of the sheet holds two separately framed parts (a strip of Newton Avenue west of town and an inset of Clove Avenue with Payne and Medina Roads) which are not part of this area. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper left.
notes: Medina Rd appears to be today's Highland Avenue; Harrison Av is Harrison Street.
The modern Bank Street / Clove Avenue / Main Street node was not detected and was hand-picked at the centre of the drawn fork.
Grant / Harrison was rejected (7.6 m from the fit).

Map, 100 ft to an inch, three parts divided by heavy lines. Part 1 (main): Clove Av, Main, Bank, Spring, Church, Unionville Av, Grant, Harrison Av, E. Main, Liberty, Pond Way. Part 2 (top strip): Newton Av west of town with block 109 and two not-named streets. Part 3 (outlined polygon): Clove Av, Payne Rd and Medina Rd north of town. Parts 2 and 3 not placed (see unplaced).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: strip along Newton Av west of town (block 109, two not-named streets) (at most one modern junction (Newton Av / Elizabeth Av, if the right-hand not-named street is Elizabeth Av), and the drawn line of Newton Av (straight across the page) cannot be reconciled with the strip's own north arrow (about -50 deg, which would make the road run NW-SE); needs identification of the road and the not-named streets on the ground, then an anchored part (px_per_ft 3.93) or parcel-corner points (step 6b)).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: outlined inset: Clove Av, Payne Rd and Medina Rd north of town (blocks 1 and 5, ice pond) (Payne Rd / Medina Rd read as Torel Road / Highland Avenue give a fit rotated 21 deg from the sheet and the inset's north arrow, with modern Clove Avenue and Highland Avenue crossing the drawn roads; with the sheet rotation the Payne Rd junctions miss the modern ones by about 85 m. Payne Rd may not survive on its 1924 line.; needs parcel-corner or house-lot control along Clove Avenue (step 6b) and a check of where Payne Rd ran).

sheet-3.description: The business centre of Sussex at 50 feet to an inch, centred on Main Street between Spring Street and Harrison Avenue. Brick and frame stores line Main Street, among them Morrison's Hotel, the post office, a bowling alley and public library, the Sussex Inn, stores with lodge rooms and offices above, a moving picture theatre, the Sussex Independent printing office and garages and auto repair shops. Newton Avenue leaves Main Street south-westward, crossing Clove Creek on an iron bridge past the Wantage Recorder newspaper office and the Horton and Lewis creamery and ice house; Bank and Spring streets and the Methodist Episcopal church lie to the north-west. To the east, Unionville Avenue, De Camp Place, the Sussex public school and its yard, Harrison Avenue, Liberty and East Main Street, with the fire department's hook and ladder house on Main Street at Harrison Avenue. Mill Street curves south from Main Street to Walling Avenue and Loomis Avenue, where the Sussex Garage and a repair shop stand by the creek and the Lehigh and New England Railroad enters at the lower right. Farm Lane and a head race run west from Newton Avenue. Clove Creek crosses the lower left of the sheet, which is otherwise largely open.
notes: Mill is today part of Loomis Avenue; the horizontal Main between Harrison Avenue and East Main is today Main Street and Hamburg Avenue.
Main Street / Spring Street was excluded: the modern node lies about 11 m from where the sheet draws it (Main north of Newton Avenue is displaced, as on deckertown-1897).
Railroad lettered L.&N.E. R.R.; abandoned today.

Map, 50 ft to an inch (fitted 7.99 px/ft). Business centre: Main, Spring, Bank, Newton Av, Church St, De Camp Pl, Unionville Av, Harrison Av, Liberty, E. Main, Mill (Loomis Av), Walling Av, Farm Lane; Clove Creek. One part.

sheet-4.description: The south-east part of Sussex at 50 feet to an inch, along Hamburg Avenue (Main) from East Main Street to beyond Brookside Avenue, and the flats south of it to Clove Creek. North of Hamburg Avenue are the First Baptist Church of Sussex with its horse shed, dwellings on East Main Street, Munson Avenue and Sutton, the Decker and Simmons lumber and coal yard with coal pockets on the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad, and the Rumsey Williams Company gas engine for sawing. South of the avenue, the F. W. and G. S. Lawrence carriage repository and implement store, a lumber shed along Walling Avenue, and the Consolidated Feed, Coal and Lumber Company by the Lehigh and New England Railroad. The railroad crosses the lower half of the sheet, with the Horton and Lewis cream company's creamery and condensery to the west, their ice house by a large ice pond, and the Sussex Mills cotton towel factory at the lower right by Brookside Avenue. Clove Creek runs along the bottom of the sheet.
notes: Hamburg Av is labelled Hamburg Av. (Main); today Hamburg Avenue (NJ 23).
Munson Av is today Munson Street.
East Main Street / Hamburg Avenue was hand-picked midway between the drawn edges; the detector had placed it on the east edge of East Main (about 6 m off).

Map, 50 ft to an inch (fitted 7.9 to 8.1 px/ft). E. Main, Munson Av, Sutton, Hamburg Av (Main), Walling Av, Brookside Av; L.&N.E. R.R., Sussex Mills, Horton & Lewis creamery, Ice Pond, Clove Creek. One part.
